parsed.rationale: All five members in package `MusicShareKit` are `type-alias-object` declarations with identical structural shape (`shared_field_count: 1`, `differing_slots: null`) and no distinguishing fields, yet they carry distinct domain names (AppleMusicService, BandcampService, SoundCloudService, SpotifyService, YouTubeMusicService). This pattern — same shape, different service identity — is the canonical use-case for a Protocol with Associated Types (PAT): introduce a `MusicService` protocol that each concrete service type conforms to, replacing the five parallel type-alias objects with a single abstraction. Because the cluster is flagged `exact-duplicates` with `jaccard: null` and empty `fields_or_signature` arrays on every member, there is no evidence of intentional specialization; the duplication appears purely structural. Consolidating under a PAT also enables generic consumers to operate over any `MusicService` without importing service-specific types.
